records.context: The window is frameless and the menu bar is what you drag it by. Its first backing store is filled with the splash colour so the compositor cannot expose stale desktop pixels before anything has drawn -- deliberately without ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent``, which is a promise to paint every pixel that this window cannot keep once the application stylesheet clears ``autoFillBackground`` again. Claiming it left whatever was already on application view underneath, and transparent children drew on top: overlapping text in the corner, and flicker on every text surface over the animated backdrop.
records.label: spacr.qt.app.MainWindow#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The window is frameless and the menu bar is what you drag it by. Its first backing store is filled with the splash colour so the compositor cannot expose stale desktop pixels before anything has drawn -- deliberately without ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent``, which is a promise to paint every pixel that this window cannot keep once the application stylesheet clears ``autoFillBackground`` again. Claiming it left whatever was already on screen underneath, and transparent children drew on top: overlapping text in the corner, and flicker on every text surface over the animated backdrop.
records.translation: La ventana no tiene marco y la barra de menús es lo que se arrastra para moverla. Su primer búfer de respaldo se rellena con el color de la pantalla de bienvenida para que el compositor no pueda mostrar píxeles obsoletos del escritorio antes de que se haya dibujado nada, deliberadamente sin ``WA_OpaquePaintEvent``, que es una promesa de pintar cada píxel que esta ventana no puede cumplir una vez que la hoja de estilos de la aplicación vuelve a desactivar ``autoFillBackground``. Declararlo dejaba debajo lo que ya hubiera en pantalla, y los hijos transparentes dibujaban encima: texto superpuesto en la esquina y parpadeo en todas las superficies de texto sobre el fondo animado.

records.source: ``"up"`` maximises (the platform's own maximised state, inside the work area that excludes the taskbar, dock or panels); ``"left"`` and ``"right"`` take the left or right half and ``"down"`` the lower half of :meth:`QScreen.availableGeometry`. Full screen is a separate state (:meth:`toggle_fullscreen`) and is left first if it is on. Work areas are in logical pixels, so display scaling is Qt's.
records.translation: ``"up"`` maximiza (el propio estado maximizado de la plataforma, dentro del área de trabajo que excluye la barra de tareas, el dock o los paneles); ``"left"`` y ``"right"`` ocupan la mitad izquierda o derecha y ``"down"`` la mitad inferior de :meth:`QScreen.availableGeometry`. La pantalla completa es un estado aparte (:meth:`toggle_fullscreen`) y, si está activa, se abandona primero. Las áreas de trabajo están en píxeles lógicos, así que el escalado de pantalla corre a cargo de Qt.

records.context: On Wayland a client cannot place its own top-level window: the half tiles are applied as a size and the compositor decides the position, so they report ``False``. records.translation: En Wayland un cliente no puede colocar su propia ventana de nivel superior: los mosaicos de media pantalla se aplican como un tamaño y el compositor decide la posición, así que informan ``False``. records.context: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every independent execution path in this application executes Python. A cancelled independent execution path that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``QThread.terminate()`` is ``pthread_cancel`` under the covers, and every thread in this application runs Python. A cancelled thread that happened to hold the GIL never releases it and the whole process stops making progress; one cancelled inside a Qt or PySide internal leaves a corrupt heap and the process dies later, somewhere unrelated. Neither failure names the line that caused it, which is why :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documents "refuse to destroy the GUI rather than use ``QThread.terminate()``" — this function is how a caller does that.
records.translation: ``QThread.terminate()`` es ``pthread_cancel`` por debajo, y todos los hilos de esta aplicación ejecutan Python. Un hilo cancelado que tuviera el GIL en ese momento nunca lo libera y todo el proceso deja de avanzar; uno cancelado dentro de una función interna de Qt o PySide deja el montículo dañado y el proceso muere más tarde, en algún lugar sin relación. Ninguno de los dos fallos señala la línea que lo causó, y por eso :meth:`RunRegistry.cancel_all` documenta "negarse a destruir la GUI antes que usar ``QThread.terminate()``"; esta función es la forma en que un llamador lo hace.

records.context: The slot is queued onto the main GUI execution path, so it executes *after* the OS independent execution path has gone. ``make_thread`` also wires ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, and the same pump that delivers this call flushes that deferred delete first — so ``isRunning()`` raises ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` from inside a Qt slot. The list comprehension never completes and **every** pair is retained, forever, along with its worker.
records.label: spacr.qt.bridge.prune_job_pairs#2

records.source: The slot is queued onto the GUI thread, so it runs *after* the OS thread has gone. ``make_thread`` also wires ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, and the same pump that delivers this call flushes that deferred delete first — so ``isRunning()`` raises ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` from inside a Qt slot. The list comprehension never completes and **every** pair is retained, forever, along with its worker.
records.translation: El slot se pone en cola en el hilo de la GUI, así que se ejecuta *después* de que el hilo del sistema operativo haya desaparecido. ``make_thread`` también conecta ``thread.finished -> thread.deleteLater``, y el mismo ciclo que entrega esta llamada ejecuta antes esa eliminación diferida, de modo que ``isRunning()`` lanza ``RuntimeError: Internal C++ object already deleted`` desde dentro de un slot de Qt. La comprensión de lista nunca termina y se conservan **todos** los pares, para siempre, junto con su hilo de trabajo.

records.translation: El vaciado de ``aboutToQuit`` de la aplicación y el gancho de salida del intérprete terminan ambos aquí. ``aboutToQuit`` solo se dispara cuando termina un bucle de eventos, así que un proceso que construye ventanas y luego simplemente termina (un script, un subproceso de prueba, una ejecución de captura que vuelve antes de tiempo) nunca lo ve, y los QThreads que iniciaron sus widgets se destruyen durante el desmontaje del intérprete mientras siguen ejecutándose. Everything between — climbing from the dropped path to the project root, asking the registry, falling back to the declared layout, noticing that the answer is ambiguous — is :func:`spacr.chaining.resolve_drop`.
records.translation: Una subclase indica dos cosas: los términos del vocabulario que consume (:attr:`kinds`, de :data:`spacr.ports.ALL_KINDS`) y qué hacer con la respuesta (:meth:`deliver`). Todo lo intermedio (subir desde la ruta soltada hasta la raíz del proyecto, consultar el registro, recurrir a la estructura declarada, detectar que la respuesta es ambigua) es :func:`spacr.chaining.resolve_drop`.

records.context: Ambiguity is routed through the machinery :mod:`spacr.qt.dnd` already has: an ambiguous drop reports ``can_accept() is False`` and returns the candidates from :meth:`suggest_alternatives`, so the user gets the "did you mean…" chooser and :meth:`apply` is called again with their answer. A drop that resolves to nothing reports :attr:`spacr.chaining.DropResolution.reason`, which is :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready`'s own sentence about what is missing.
records.label: spacr.qt.dnd_handlers.LayoutDropHandler#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Ambiguity is routed through the machinery :mod:`spacr.qt.dnd` already has: an ambiguous drop reports ``can_accept() is False`` and returns the candidates from :meth:`suggest_alternatives`, so the user gets the "did you mean…" chooser and :meth:`apply` is called again with their answer. A drop that resolves to nothing reports :attr:`spacr.chaining.DropResolution.reason`, which is :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready`'s own sentence about what is missing.
records.translation: La ambigüedad se canaliza a través de los mecanismos que :mod:`spacr.qt.dnd` ya tiene: un soltado ambiguo informa ``can_accept() is False`` y devuelve los candidatos de :meth:`suggest_alternatives`, de modo que el usuario obtiene el selector "did you mean…" (¿quiso decir…?) y :meth:`apply` se vuelve a llamar con su respuesta. Un soltado que no se resuelve en nada informa :attr:`spacr.chaining.DropResolution.reason`, que es la propia frase de :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` sobre lo que falta.

records.context: The two differ in exactly one place, and it matters only there. A block registered with :func:`register_widget_qss` is handed the ``opacity`` :func:`stylesheet` was called with, and that is ``None`` when the caller asked for the theme's *designed* scrim rather than any user's setting — the documented meaning of ``surface_opacity=None``, and what every built-in rule in this file honours through :func:`panel_alpha`.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The two differ in exactly one place, and it matters only there. A block registered with :func:`register_widget_qss` is handed the ``opacity`` :func:`stylesheet` was called with, and that is ``None`` when the caller asked for the theme's *designed* scrim rather than any user's setting — the documented meaning of ``surface_opacity=None``, and what every built-in rule in this file honours through :func:`panel_alpha`.
records.translation: Las dos difieren exactamente en un punto, y solo importa ahí. Un bloque registrado con :func:`register_widget_qss` recibe el ``opacity`` con el que se llamó a :func:`stylesheet`, y este es ``None`` cuando quien llama pidió el velo *diseñado* del tema en lugar del ajuste de cualquier usuario: el significado documentado de ``surface_opacity=None``, y lo que respetan todas las reglas integradas de este archivo mediante :func:`panel_alpha`.

records.context: :func:`pane_surface` cannot honour it. Its ``None`` means "nobody told me, go and look", so it reads the live page-opacity preference. That is right for the inline and paint-time callers it was written for — Home's aside panels have no ``stylesheet`` argument to plumb through — and wrong inside a block, where ``None`` was already an answer. The consequence was that ``stylesheet("dark")`` emitted ``rgba(22, 23, 25, 0.600)`` for every block that passed it through: a function of its arguments quietly depending on a QSettings value, which made the assertion that the opaque themes emit plain hex pass or fail on module import order.

records.source: The application stylesheet scales :data:`FONT_SIZE` itself (see :func:`stylesheet`), so anything styled by it already tracks Zoom. What does *not* is a widget that sets its own sheet — a per-widget ``setStyleSheet`` beats the application sheet whatever the selector says — or one that paints text with a ``QPainter``. Those surfaces hard-coded a pixel number and so stayed 13 px at 150 %: the tab strips, the Home aside, the hover tooltip, the Live/AI toggles.
records.translation: La hoja de estilos de la aplicación escala :data:`FONT_SIZE` por sí misma (véase :func:`stylesheet`), de modo que todo lo que recibe estilo de ella ya sigue a Zoom. Lo que *no* lo hace es un widget que establece su propia hoja (un ``setStyleSheet`` por widget prevalece sobre la hoja de la aplicación diga lo que diga el selector) o uno que pinta texto con un ``QPainter``. Esas superficies tenían un número de píxeles fijo en el código y por eso se quedaban en 13 px al 150 %: las tiras de pestañas, el panel lateral de Home, la información emergente al pasar el cursor y los conmutadores Live/AI.

Rules naming the ``bg`` surface are judged against it directly, because in an image theme nothing is painted between the photograph and the text. Everything else is judged against its scrim composited over it.
records.translation: ``under`` es un color muestreado del fondo de pantalla; en la práctica, la media de su región más brillante del tamaño de una línea de texto, que es lo que devuelve :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window`. Las reglas que nombran la superficie ``bg`` se evalúan directamente frente a él, porque en un tema de imagen no se pinta nada entre la fotografía y el texto. Todo lo demás se evalúa frente a su velo compuesto sobre él.

records.source: A backdrop — the theme's wallpaper, or the DNA rain on the sequencing screen — is behind the *page*, and in the opaque themes every container between it and the eye is an opaque ``bg`` by virtue of the blanket ``QWidget`` rule. One container is enough to bury it: a screen's header widget, its splitter, a scroll area and that scroll area's viewport are each a QWidget, and each one used to paint solid black over the animation the screen had just installed.
records.translation: Un fondo (el fondo de pantalla del tema, o la lluvia de DNA en la pantalla de secuenciación) está detrás de la *página*, y en los temas opacos todos los contenedores entre él y el ojo son un ``bg`` opaco en virtud de la regla general de ``QWidget``. Basta un contenedor para taparlo: el widget de cabecera de una pantalla, su divisor, un área de desplazamiento y la ventana gráfica de esa área son cada uno un QWidget, y cada uno pintaba antes negro sólido sobre la animación que la pantalla acababa de instalar.

records.context: Tag the layout containers with this and the backdrop reaches the eye; leave the cards, panels and inputs alone and they stay the readable surface on top of it. Safe to call on a widget that is already visible — the style is re-polished so the change takes effect immediately rather than at the next theme switch. A widget no stylesheet reaches yet, or one in a window whose sheet is held (:func:`_one_sheet_for`), is only tagged: nothing reads the tag until a sheet arrives, and putting a sheet on polishes every widget it reaches. Glassing Preferences tags about 400 containers, and polishing each one before its sheet went on cost 53-64 ms for nothing.

records.translation: Marque con esto los contenedores de diseño y el fondo llegará al ojo; deje intactas las tarjetas, los paneles y las entradas, y seguirán siendo la superficie legible por encima. Se puede llamar sin riesgo sobre un widget que ya es visible: el estilo se vuelve a pulir para que el cambio surta efecto de inmediato y no en el siguiente cambio de tema. Un widget al que todavía no llega ninguna hoja de estilos, o uno en una ventana cuya hoja está retenida (:func:`_one_sheet_for`), solo se marca: nada lee la marca hasta que llega una hoja, y aplicar una hoja pule todos los widgets a los que llega. Aplicar el efecto de vidrio a Preferences marca unos 400 contenedores, y pulir cada uno antes de que se aplicara su hoja costaba 53-64 ms para nada.

records.translation: Dos pantallas ya expresaban esto antes de que existiera el mecanismo, dando a la vista un nombre de objeto y registrando todo un bloque QSS para ella: las tablas de resultados de Model Compare y el listado y el cuadro de procedencia de Model Zoo. records.context: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. Measured both ways rather than reasoned about.

records.source: One Qt rule has to be paid on the way. A **subclass** of ``QWidget`` ignores a QSS background entirely unless ``WA_StyledBackground`` is set, which is why Power's caveat panel still measured the backdrop untouched with a matching rule sitting in the sheet. The attribute is set here for those, and deliberately NOT for a ``QAbstractScrollArea``: a view already paints its background through its viewport, and a second styled fill on top of that is the two-surfaces-stacked fault again. Measured both ways rather than reasoned about.
records.translation: Hay que cumplir una regla de Qt por el camino. Una **subclase** de ``QWidget`` ignora por completo un fondo QSS a menos que se establezca ``WA_StyledBackground``, y por eso el panel de advertencias de Power seguía midiendo el fondo intacto aunque había una regla coincidente en la hoja. El atributo se establece aquí para esos casos, y deliberadamente NO para un ``QAbstractScrollArea``: una vista ya pinta su fondo a través de su ventana gráfica, y un segundo relleno con estilo encima vuelve a ser el fallo de dos superficies apiladas. Se midió de ambas formas en lugar de razonarlo.

records.context: **Cell** wallpapers always come out of :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.render`, which exposure-solves every frame it returns — the shipped masters and the user's own drop-in alike. No text-line-sized region of a Cell background can therefore exceed :func:`max_background_luma`, and that ceiling, not white, is the worst case a Cell panel has to survive. Measured: the shipped ``microtubules`` master peaks at 0.098 against a 0.109 limit, ``filopodia`` at 0.073.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.scrim_under#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Cell** wallpapers always come out of :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.render`, which exposure-solves every frame it returns — the shipped masters and the user's own drop-in alike. No text-line-sized region of a Cell background can therefore exceed :func:`max_background_luma`, and that ceiling, not white, is the worst case a Cell panel has to survive. Measured: the shipped ``microtubules`` master peaks at 0.098 against a 0.109 limit, ``filopodia`` at 0.073.
records.translation: Los fondos de pantalla de **Cell** siempre salen de :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.render`, que ajusta la exposición de cada fotograma que devuelve, tanto los originales incluidos como los que aporta el propio usuario. Por tanto, ninguna región del tamaño de una línea de texto de un fondo de Cell puede superar :func:`max_background_luma`, y ese techo, no el blanco, es el peor caso que debe soportar un panel de Cell. Medido: el original incluido ``microtubules`` alcanza un máximo de 0.098 frente a un límite de 0.109, y ``filopodia``, de 0.073.

records.context: **Space** can be the procedurally generated sky, whose exposure is anchored on the 40th percentile *precisely so a sun stays white-hot* (:data:`spacr.qt.space.TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE`). That is a deliberate look, and it means the sky really does present a near-white region the size of a line of text: the 1440x900 galaxy sky measures 0.49 over a text window, colour ``#bab9b9``. Only a strong scrim saves text over that, so Space is judged against white and its panels stay much more opaque than Cell's.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.scrim_under#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Space** can be the procedurally generated sky, whose exposure is anchored on the 40th percentile *precisely so a sun stays white-hot* (:data:`spacr.qt.space.TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE`). That is a deliberate look, and it means the sky really does present a near-white region the size of a line of text: the 1440x900 galaxy sky measures 0.49 over a text window, colour ``#bab9b9``. Only a strong scrim saves text over that, so Space is judged against white and its panels stay much more opaque than Cell's.
records.translation: **Space** puede ser el cielo generado por procedimientos, cuya exposición se ancla en el percentil 40 *precisamente para que un sol siga al rojo blanco* (:data:`spacr.qt.space.TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE`). Es un aspecto deliberado, y significa que el cielo presenta realmente una región casi blanca del tamaño de una línea de texto: el cielo de galaxia de 1440x900 mide 0.49 en una ventana de texto, color ``#bab9b9``. Solo un velo intenso salva el texto sobre eso, así que Space se evalúa frente al blanco y sus paneles se mantienen mucho más opacos que los de Cell.

records.context: For a widget that is a sheet root. Before per-application view sheeting, a module application view's own stylesheet held only its own rules and the APPLICATION carried the theme, so `setStyleSheet` on the application view was a safe, local thing to do. Now the application view may be carrying all ~73 KB of the window sheet, and a plain `setStyleSheet` throws the theme away.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.set_a_sheeted_widgets_own_rule#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: FOR A WIDGET THAT IS A SHEET ROOT. Before per-screen sheeting, a module screen's own stylesheet held only its own rules and the APPLICATION carried the theme, so `setStyleSheet` on the screen was a safe, local thing to do. Now the screen may be carrying all ~73 KB of the window sheet, and a plain `setStyleSheet` throws the theme away.
records.translation: PARA UN WIDGET QUE ES RAÍZ DE HOJA. Antes de aplicar hojas por pantalla, la hoja de estilos propia de una pantalla de módulo contenía solo sus propias reglas y la APLICACIÓN llevaba el tema, así que `setStyleSheet` sobre la pantalla era algo seguro y local. Ahora la pantalla puede llevar los ~73 KB completos de la hoja de la ventana, y un simple `setStyleSheet` descarta el tema.

records.context: The answer is the ceiling, clamped up to the floor: as solid a panel as the picture can afford, and never thinner than legibility allows. Every alpha in that window satisfies both constraints, so the choice within it is which one to spend the slack on, and it goes to the panel: the settings form sits on this surface, and preserving its grey category structure is more important than exposing additional wallpaper. Taking the floor instead would show *more* picture — Cell's floor is 0.05, a nearly transparent panel — at the cost of the form dissolving into the wallpaper.
records.label: spacr.qt.theme.solve_scrim_alpha#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The answer is the ceiling, clamped up to the floor: as solid a panel as the picture can afford, and never thinner than legibility allows. Every alpha in that window satisfies both constraints, so the choice within it is which one to spend the slack on, and it goes to the panel: the settings form sits on this surface, and preserving its grey category structure is more important than exposing additional wallpaper. Taking the floor instead would show *more* picture — Cell's floor is 0.05, a nearly transparent panel — at the cost of the form dissolving into the wallpaper.
records.translation: La respuesta es el techo, elevado como mínimo hasta el suelo: un panel tan sólido como la imagen pueda permitirse, y nunca más fino de lo que permite la legibilidad. Todos los valores alfa de ese intervalo cumplen ambas restricciones, así que la elección dentro de él consiste en a qué dedicar el margen, y se le da al panel: el formulario de ajustes está sobre esta superficie, y conservar su estructura gris de categorías es más importante que mostrar más fondo de pantalla. Tomar el suelo mostraría *más* imagen (el suelo de Cell es 0.05, un panel casi transparente) a costa de que el formulario se disuelva en el fondo de pantalla.

records.context: When the floor lands *above* the ceiling the theme cannot do both, legibility wins, and the shortfall is visible in :func:`scrim_report`.

records.source: When the floor lands *above* the ceiling the theme cannot do both, legibility wins, and the shortfall is visible in :func:`scrim_report`.
records.translation: Cuando el suelo queda *por encima* del techo, el tema no puede cumplir ambas cosas, la legibilidad prevalece y el déficit se ve en :func:`scrim_report`.

records.context: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` selects the objects and records the selection reason; this module resolves and displays their extracted image regions beside the processing session's figures. Each attached database resolves its own exported-PNG or ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source so multi-plate montages can combine experiments with different storage layouts. The extracted image region mask image layer and image data channels come from :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` or, by default, the processing session's ``measurements.db`` metadata.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.cell_montage_view#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` selects the objects and records the selection reason; this module resolves and displays their image crops beside the run's figures. Each attached database resolves its own exported-PNG or ``merged/<fov>.npy`` source so multi-plate montages can combine experiments with different storage layouts. The crop mask plane and channels come from :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` or, by default, the run's ``measurements.db`` metadata.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.cell_montage` selecciona los objetos y registra el motivo de la selección; este módulo resuelve y muestra sus recortes de imagen junto a las figuras de la ejecución. Cada base de datos asociada resuelve su propio origen de PNG exportado o de ``merged/<fov>.npy``, de modo que los montajes de varias placas pueden combinar experimentos con distintas estructuras de almacenamiento. El plano de máscara y los canales del recorte proceden de :class:`spacr.crops.CropSpec` o, por defecto, de los metadatos de ``measurements.db`` de la ejecución.

records.translation: La pestaña sigue visible cuando no hay recortes disponibles e informa del motivo en su estado, en su información emergente y en la acción desactivada. records.source: Three properties this file is built around:
records.translation: Tres propiedades en torno a las que se construye este archivo:

records.context: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
records.translation: **Solo lectura.** Abrir el selector lee los nombres de las columnas y nada más. La conexión es ``file:…?mode=ro`` más ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` (el mismo par que usan :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` y :mod:`spacr.agreement`), de modo que el propio SQLite rechaza cualquier escritura. El cuadro de diálogo nunca crea una columna: devuelve un *nombre*, y la vía de escritura responsable de la creación (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, que lo hace de forma diferida con ``ALTER TABLE``) se queda donde está.

records.context: **Cheap on open.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` is free; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` over a 400 k-row measurement table is not. Opening the dialog runs no count at all. The per-table row figure comes from ``max(_rowid_)`` and is labelled an estimate; a per-column non-null count happens only when the user asks for it by name. (``_rowid_``, not ``rowid`` — see :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, where the difference was a full table scan followed by a ``ValueError``.)
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Cheap on open.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` is free; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` over a 400 k-row measurement table is not. Opening the dialog runs no count at all. The per-table row figure comes from ``max(_rowid_)`` and is labelled an estimate; a per-column non-null count happens only when the user asks for it by name. (``_rowid_``, not ``rowid`` — see :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, where the difference was a full table scan followed by a ``ValueError``.)
records.translation: **Barato al abrirse.** ``PRAGMA table_info`` es gratuito; ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` sobre una tabla de mediciones de 400 k filas no lo es. Abrir el cuadro de diálogo no ejecuta ningún recuento. La cifra de filas por tabla procede de ``max(_rowid_)`` y se etiqueta como estimación; un recuento de valores no nulos por columna solo se realiza cuando el usuario lo pide por su nombre. (``_rowid_``, no ``rowid``; véase :meth:`SchemaReader.estimate_rows`, donde la diferencia era un recorrido completo de la tabla seguido de un ``ValueError``.)

records.context: **Background loading.** The picker does not freeze the GUI. It performs four sequential sqlite queries: open, list tables, read one table's columns, and estimate its rows. Previously, before a dialog appeared, all four queries ran in ``__init__``. Cold measurements were 45 ms for measurements.db, a 383 MB database, and 87 ms for a schema with 1 500 tables. The dialog now selects background mode with ``threaded=True``. All reads are performed by :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. Synchronous mode remains the initial choice; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` explains why.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Off the GUI thread.** Cheap is not free, and opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips — open, list tables, read one table's columns, estimate its rows — every one of which used to happen inside ``__init__``, before the modal appeared. Measured cold on a 383 MB measurements.db that is 45 ms, and on a 1 500-table schema 87 ms, entirely between the click and any window. The button now builds the dialog with ``threaded=True`` and the reads arrive from a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. The default is still the synchronous mode, deliberately; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` says why.
records.translation: **Fuera del hilo de la GUI.** Barato no es gratuito, y abrir el selector supone cuatro idas y vueltas secuenciales a sqlite (abrir, listar tablas, leer las columnas de una tabla, estimar sus filas), y todas ellas ocurrían antes dentro de ``__init__``, antes de que apareciera el modal. Medido en frío sobre un measurements.db de 383 MB, son 45 ms, y sobre un esquema de 1 500 tablas, 87 ms, todo entre el clic y la aparición de cualquier ventana. Ahora el botón construye el cuadro de diálogo con ``threaded=True`` y las lecturas llegan desde un :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. El valor por defecto sigue siendo el modo síncrono, deliberadamente; :class:`ColumnPickerDialog` explica por qué.

records.context: ``threaded=False`` (the default) reads the schema inside ``__init__``: when the constructor returns, the tables are listed, a table is selected, its columns are in the tree and the name box has been judged. records.translation: ``threaded=False`` (el valor por defecto) lee el esquema dentro de ``__init__``: cuando el constructor termina, las tablas están listadas, hay una tabla seleccionada, sus columnas están en el árbol y el cuadro de nombre ya se ha evaluado. Para eso están escritos todos los llamadores programáticos y las ~60 pruebas de ``tests/qt/test_column_picker.py``: construyen un cuadro de diálogo y hacen aserciones sobre su contenido en la línea siguiente, sin ningún bucle de eventos (el fixture autouse de la suite hace que ``QDialog.exec`` lance una excepción). Usar por defecto el modo asíncrono convertiría cada una de ellas en una condición de carrera, así que es opcional.

records.context: ``threaded=True`` is what the ``SQL`` button uses (:meth:`ColumnPickerButton.make_dialog`), and it is the real user-facing path. The window appears immediately saying it is reading the schema, and the tables, columns and row estimate arrive from a :class:`~spacr.qt.job_runner.JobRunner`. That matters because opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips against a file that is usually cold and often on a network mount — measured at 45 ms on a 383 MB measurements.db with nothing cached and 87 ms on a 1 500-table schema, all of it dead time between the click and the window.

That matters because opening the picker is four sequential sqlite round trips against a file that is usually cold and often on a network mount — measured at 45 ms on a 383 MB measurements.db with nothing cached and 87 ms on a 1 500-table schema, all of it dead time between the click and the window.
records.translation: ``threaded=True`` es lo que usa el botón ``SQL`` (:meth:`ColumnPickerButton.make_dialog`), y es la verdadera vía de cara al usuario. Esto importa porque abrir el selector supone cuatro idas y vueltas secuenciales a sqlite sobre un archivo que suele estar en frío y a menudo en un montaje de red: medido en 45 ms sobre un measurements.db de 383 MB sin nada en caché y en 87 ms sobre un esquema de 1 500 tablas, todo ello tiempo muerto entre el clic y la ventana.

records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker.SchemaReader.estimate_rows#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: It is spelt ``_rowid_`` for a reason. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the plate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. On a measurements database, ``max(rowid)`` scans the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table, the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method avoids), and ``int('r16')`` then raises ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and would escape the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` handle the same shadowing.
records.translation: Se escribe ``_rowid_`` por una razón. Toda tabla de objetos de spaCR declara una columna llamada ``rowID`` (la fila de la placa, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'``), y los identificadores de SQLite no distinguen mayúsculas de minúsculas, así que un ``rowid`` a secas se resuelve a *esa columna* y no al identificador de fila. En una base de datos de mediciones, ``max(rowid)`` recorre toda la tabla para obtener el máximo de una columna de texto (medido: 21 ms en caliente, 41 ms en frío, en una tabla de 200 000 filas, el coste de ``COUNT(*)`` que este método evita), y después ``int('r16')`` lanza ``ValueError``, que no es un ``sqlite3.Error`` y escaparía del controlador de quien llama hasta el bucle de eventos de Qt. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` y :mod:`spacr.data_manager` gestionan el mismo enmascaramiento.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#0
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Control-chart statistics for a screening campaign: limits, rules and Z'.
records.translation: Estadísticos de gráficos de control para una campaña de cribado: límites, reglas y Z'.

records.context: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all assume that the positive and negative controls behave the same way on every plate. When the controls drift — the cell line changes, a reagent lot changes, incubation conditions change — every downstream result shifts with them, and the analysis does not detect it, because it normalises to the controls it is given.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A screening campaign is dozens of plates run over weeks. Hit calling, plate normalisation and Z' all assume that the positive and negative controls behave the same way on every plate. When the controls drift — the cell line changes, a reagent lot changes, incubation conditions change — every downstream result shifts with them, and the analysis does not detect it, because it normalises to the controls it is given.
records.translation: Una campaña de cribado son decenas de placas procesadas a lo largo de semanas. La identificación de hits, la normalización por placa y Z' presuponen que los controles positivos y negativos se comportan igual en todas las placas. Cuando los controles derivan (cambia la línea celular, cambia un lote de reactivo, cambian las condiciones de incubación), todos los resultados posteriores se desplazan con ellos, y el análisis no lo detecta, porque normaliza respecto a los controles que recibe.

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Individuals / moving range (I-MR). One control value per laboratory microplate is the normal case in a screen, so this is what :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` picks when every laboratory microplate contributes a single control microplate sample position. Sigma is ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128``; 1.128 is d2 for a subgroup of two, which is what a moving range of consecutive points is.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Individuals / moving range (I-MR). One control value per plate is the normal case in a screen, so this is what :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` picks when every plate contributes a single control well. Sigma is ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128``; 1.128 is d2 for a subgroup of two, which is what a moving range of consecutive points is.
records.translation: :data:`ESTIMATOR_MOVING_RANGE` Valores individuales / rango móvil (I-MR). Un valor de control por placa es el caso normal en un cribado, así que esto es lo que elige :data:`ESTIMATOR_AUTO` cuando cada placa aporta un único pocillo de control. Sigma es ``mean(|x_i - x_{i-1}|) / 1.128``; 1.128 es d2 para un subgrupo de dos, que es lo que es un rango móvil de puntos consecutivos.

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_SUBGROUP_S` X-bar / S, for a laboratory microplate with several control microplate sample positions (subgroup ``n > 1``). The plotted point is the laboratory microplate's mean and sigma is ``S-bar / c4(n)``, where :func:`c4` is computed from the gamma function rather than looked up in a table. The published table stops at n = 25, does not interpolate, and is prone to transcription errors. ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)`` is three lines, is exact for every n, and can be checked against the published constant — ``c4(5) = 0.9400`` — which is what the test does.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :data:`ESTIMATOR_SUBGROUP_S` X-bar / S, for a plate with several control wells (subgroup ``n > 1``). The plotted point is the plate's mean and sigma is ``S-bar / c4(n)``, where :func:`c4` is computed from the gamma function rather than looked up in a table. The published table stops at n = 25, does not interpolate, and is prone to transcription errors. ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)`` is three lines, is exact for every n, and can be checked against the published constant — ``c4(5) = 0.9400`` — which is what the test does.
records.translation: :data:`ESTIMATOR_SUBGROUP_S` X-bar / S, para una placa con varios pocillos de control (subgrupo ``n > 1``). El punto representado es la media de la placa y sigma es ``S-bar / c4(n)``, donde :func:`c4` se calcula a partir de la función gamma en lugar de consultarse en una tabla. La tabla publicada se detiene en n = 25, no interpola y es propensa a errores de transcripción. ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)`` son tres líneas, es exacto para cualquier n y se puede comprobar con la constante publicada (``c4(5) = 0.9400``), que es lo que hace la prueba.

Cuando los tamaños de subgrupo difieren entre placas, los límites difieren por placa; se calculan por punto en lugar de promediarse, y el resultado lo indica.

records.context: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` Explicit, never implicit, and named in the result. spaCR measurements are skewed and one catastrophically bad plate inside the baseline drags the classical centre and MR-bar out far enough to swallow everything after it. The robust variant takes the **median** as the centre and either the median moving range (:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) or the MAD (:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`) as the spread.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` Explicit, never implicit, and named in the result. spaCR measurements are skewed and one catastrophically bad plate inside the baseline drags the classical centre and MR-bar out far enough to swallow everything after it. The robust variant takes the **median** as the centre and either the median moving range (:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) or the MAD (:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`) as the spread.
records.translation: :data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST` / :data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD` Explícito, nunca implícito, y nombrado en el resultado. Las mediciones de spaCR son asimétricas, y una sola placa catastróficamente mala dentro de la referencia desplaza el centro clásico y el MR-bar lo suficiente como para engullir todo lo que viene después. La variante robusta toma la **mediana** como centro y, como dispersión, el rango móvil mediano (:data:`ESTIMATOR_ROBUST`) o la MAD (:data:`ESTIMATOR_MAD`).

records.context: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.control_chart#14

records.source: The two robust constants are *not* interchangeable, and the module keeps them separate. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) is ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, the factor that makes the MAD of a normal sample an unbiased estimate of its SD. A moving range is ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, the absolute value of a *difference* of two observations, so its scale is ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` and its median is ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplying a median moving range by 1.4826 overestimates sigma by exactly ``sqrt(2)``, which makes the limits 41% wider and can hide a drift. Both constants are computed from ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` here for the same reason c4 is computed from the gamma function.
records.translation: Las dos constantes robustas *no* son intercambiables, y el módulo las mantiene separadas. 1.4826 (:data:`MAD_SCALE`) es ``1/Φ⁻¹(0.75)``, el factor que hace que la MAD de una muestra normal sea un estimador insesgado de su SD. Un rango móvil es ``|x_i - x_{i-1}|``, el valor absoluto de una *diferencia* de dos observaciones, así que su escala es ``sqrt(2)·sigma`` y su mediana es ``sqrt(2)·Φ⁻¹(0.75)·sigma = 0.9539·sigma`` (:data:`MEDIAN_MR_CONSTANT`). Multiplicar un rango móvil mediano por 1.4826 sobrestima sigma exactamente en ``sqrt(2)``, lo que hace los límites un 41% más anchos y puede ocultar una deriva. Ambas constantes se calculan aquí a partir de ``Φ⁻¹(0.75)`` por la misma razón por la que c4 se calcula a partir de la función gamma.

records.context: The baseline is the first :data:`DEFAULT_BASELINE` laboratory microplates in run order by default (twenty, the textbook Phase I minimum for an individuals chart), or an explicit list of laboratory microplate ids (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.baseline_plates`), or everything before a cut-off in the order column (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.baseline_before`). Whichever it was, the plates that formed it are in :attr:`ControlChartResult.baseline_plates` and named in :meth:`ControlChartResult.report`.
records.translation: Por defecto, la referencia son las primeras :data:`DEFAULT_BASELINE` placas en el orden de procesamiento (veinte, el mínimo de manual de la Fase I para un gráfico de valores individuales), o una lista explícita de identificadores de placa (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.baseline_plates`), o todo lo anterior a un punto de corte en la columna de orden (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.baseline_before`). Sea cual sea, las placas que la formaron están en :attr:`ControlChartResult.baseline_plates` y se nombran en :meth:`ControlChartResult.report`.

records.context: :data:`MIN_BASELINE` is eight, because MR-bar over seven moving ranges is already dominated by one or two plate-to-plate jumps, and with fewer by one. A shorter baseline is refused.

records.translation: :data:`MIN_BASELINE` es ocho, porque el MR-bar sobre siete rangos móviles ya está dominado por uno o dos saltos entre placas, y con menos, por uno solo. Una referencia más corta se rechaza.

records.context: **Limits estimated from an out-of-control baseline are unreliable.** When the baseline itself contains a violation, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` says so. Re-estimating without the flagged plates is *offered* (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) and is off by default, so plates are never removed from the baseline without the user asking. It runs one pass, not iterations to convergence: iterating shrinks the limits onto the tightest subset of the baseline and eventually flags everything.

records.source: **Limits estimated from an out-of-control baseline are unreliable.** When the baseline itself contains a violation, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` says so. Re-estimating without the flagged plates is *offered* (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) and is off by default, so plates are never removed from the baseline without the user asking. It runs one pass, not iterations to convergence: iterating shrinks the limits onto the tightest subset of the baseline and eventually flags everything.
records.translation: **Los límites estimados a partir de una referencia fuera de control no son fiables.** Cuando la propia referencia contiene una infracción, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` lo indica. Volver a estimar sin las placas señaladas se *ofrece* (:attr:`ControlChartSpec.reestimate`) y está desactivado por defecto, de modo que nunca se eliminan placas de la referencia sin que el usuario lo pida. Se ejecuta una sola pasada, no iteraciones hasta la convergencia: iterar contrae los límites sobre el subconjunto más ajustado de la referencia y acaba señalándolo todo.

records.context: This module tracks one control value per plate over run order and puts limits round it, so drift is visible while the application view is running rather than after. It is pure numpy/pandas — no Qt anywhere in it, the same rule :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec` and :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` follow — so it is usable from a notebook, testable without a display, and free for a report or a QC data-selection boundary to call.

records.context: The rule set is selectable, and it has to be, because **running all eight is not eight times the sensitivity**. Each rule has its own in-control false-alarm rate; :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE` carries them, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` does the arithmetic for the set that actually ran, and over a 200-plate campaign it reports the expected number of false alarms. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT` is the Western Electric four (1, 2, 5, 6), which is the set the classical ARL figure was worked out for; :data:`RULES_ALL` is all eight, and :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY` is rule 1 alone for a user who wants limits and nothing else.

Each rule has its own in-control false-alarm rate; :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE` carries them, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` does the arithmetic for the set that actually ran, and over a 200-plate campaign it reports the expected number of false alarms. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT` is the Western Electric four (1, 2, 5, 6), which is the set the classical ARL figure was worked out for; :data:`RULES_ALL` is all eight, and :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY` is rule 1 alone for a user who wants limits and nothing else.
records.translation: El conjunto de reglas es seleccionable, y tiene que serlo, porque **ejecutar las ocho no multiplica por ocho la sensibilidad**. Cada regla tiene su propia tasa de falsas alarmas bajo control; :data:`RULE_ALARM_RATE` las contiene, :meth:`ControlChartResult.caveats` hace las cuentas para el conjunto que realmente se ejecutó y, para una campaña de 200 placas, informa del número esperado de falsas alarmas. :data:`RULES_DEFAULT` son las cuatro de Western Electric (1, 2, 5, 6), que es el conjunto para el que se calculó la cifra ARL clásica; :data:`RULES_ALL` son las ocho, y :data:`RULES_LIMITS_ONLY` es solo la regla 1, para un usuario que quiere límites y nada más.

records.context: ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)``, which is ``E[s] / sigma`` for a normal sample of size ``n``: the sample SD is a biased estimate of sigma, badly so for the small subgroups a laboratory microplate's control microplate sample positions make, and ``S-bar / c4(n)`` is the correction.

records.translation: ``c4(n) = sqrt(2/(n-1)) · Γ(n/2) / Γ((n-1)/2)``, que es ``E[s] / sigma`` para una muestra normal de tamaño ``n``: la SD muestral es un estimador sesgado de sigma, muy sesgado para los subgrupos pequeños que forman los pocillos de control de una placa, y ``S-bar / c4(n)`` es la corrección.

records.context: The casing is load-bearing; the orientation is what makes it part of the rain. It used to be stored as a single token in a single cell and drawn horizontally, overflowing rightwards across its neighbours — which read as a label pasted over the effect rather than as part of it, and cost the renderer a whole second paint pass, measured token widths, widened dirty rectangles and a cleared backing rectangle so neighbouring glyphs did not tangle with the letters. None of that machinery exists now: every cell holds exactly one character, so the word is cached and blitted like any other glyph and cannot overdraw anything. See :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` for the rate and what it works out to in practice.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dna_rain#12
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The casing is load-bearing; the orientation is what makes it part of the rain. It used to be stored as a single token in a single cell and drawn horizontally, overflowing rightwards across its neighbours — which read as a label pasted over the effect rather than as part of it, and cost the renderer a whole second paint pass, measured token widths, widened dirty rectangles and a cleared backing rectangle so neighbouring glyphs did not tangle with the letters. None of that machinery exists now: every cell holds exactly one character, so the word is cached and blitted like any other glyph and cannot overdraw anything. See :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` for the rate and what it works out to in practice.
records.translation: Las mayúsculas y minúsculas son esenciales; la orientación es lo que la integra en la lluvia. Antes se almacenaba como un único token en una única celda y se dibujaba en horizontal, desbordándose hacia la derecha sobre sus vecinas, lo que se leía como una etiqueta pegada encima del efecto y no como parte de él, y costaba al renderizador una segunda pasada de pintado completa, medir anchos de token, ampliar rectángulos sucios y limpiar un rectángulo de fondo para que los glifos vecinos no se enredaran con las letras. Ahora no existe nada de esa maquinaria («None of that machinery»): cada celda contiene exactamente un carácter, así que la palabra se almacena en caché y se copia como cualquier otro glifo y no puede pintar encima de nada. Véase :data:`SPACR_SPLICE_PROBABILITY` para la frecuencia y lo que supone en la práctica.

records.context: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one application view that has a rain.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dna_rain.DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rain is an opaque backdrop by construction — it repaints only the cells that changed, so it has to be able to *clear* them, and clearing to a translucent colour smears the previous frame. That is the right trade on the dark and light themes, where the thing behind it is a flat ``bg`` the rain can reproduce exactly. On an image theme it is not: the flat colour is nothing like the wallpaper, and an opaque rain hid the photograph completely on the one screen that has a rain.
records.translation: La lluvia es un fondo opaco por construcción: solo repinta las celdas que cambiaron, así que tiene que poder *borrarlas*, y borrar con un color translúcido emborrona el fotograma anterior. Es la compensación correcta en los temas oscuro y claro, donde lo que hay detrás es un ``bg`` plano que la lluvia puede reproducir exactamente. En un tema de imagen no lo es: el color plano no se parece en nada al fondo de pantalla, y una lluvia opaca ocultaba por completo la fotografía en la única pantalla que tiene lluvia.

records.context: Handing the wallpaper in fixes that without giving up the dirty-rectangle repaint: the clear becomes a blit of the corresponding piece of the image, aligned to where the window's own stylesheet paints it, and the strips switch to per-pixel alpha so the glyphs composite over the picture instead of over a colour baked into them.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dna_rain.DnaRainWidget.set_backdrop#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Handing the wallpaper in fixes that without giving up the dirty-rectangle repaint: the clear becomes a blit of the corresponding piece of the image, aligned to where the window's own stylesheet paints it, and the strips switch to per-pixel alpha so the glyphs composite over the picture instead of over a colour baked into them.
records.translation: Proporcionar el fondo de pantalla lo soluciona sin renunciar al repintado por rectángulos sucios: el borrado se convierte en una copia del fragmento correspondiente de la imagen, alineado con el lugar donde lo pinta la hoja de estilos de la propia ventana, y las tiras pasan a usar alfa por píxel para que los glifos se compongan sobre la imagen y no sobre un color incrustado en ellos.

records.context: The cost is the one the module docstring quantifies: a translucent strip is roughly 25x more expensive to blit than an opaque one, so this path is used *only* when there is a picture to show. ``set_backdrop(None)`` puts the fast path back.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The cost is the one the module docstring quantifies: a translucent strip is roughly 25x more expensive to blit than an opaque one, so this path is used *only* when there is a picture to show. ``set_backdrop(None)`` puts the fast path back.
records.translation: El coste es el que cuantifica la docstring del módulo: una tira translúcida es aproximadamente 25x más cara de copiar que una opaca, así que esta vía se usa *solo* cuando hay una imagen que mostrar. ``set_backdrop(None)`` restablece la vía rápida.

records.source: Random colour is *per column*, and a column is one falling string among a hundred. Rolling all three HSL components would have given the field a scatter of near-blacks, near-whites and greys — most of which do not read as glyphs at 20 % opacity behind a settings form. Only the hue is random; saturation and lightness are taken from the colour in the picker, floored and clamped so the result is always a colour and always visible.
records.translation: El color aleatorio es *por columna*, y una columna es una cadena que cae entre cien. records.context: :class:`GateCanvas` subclasses :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` for the same reason :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_view.TrellisCanvas` does: the marks, the hue order, the density raster and the large-data policy are one implementation. records.translation: :class:`GateCanvas` es una subclase de :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` por la misma razón que :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.trellis_view.TrellisCanvas`: las marcas, el orden de tonos, el ráster de densidad y la política para grandes volúmenes de datos son una sola implementación. records.context: **The asymmetry problem is real and is not fixed by choosing a bigger c.** Tukey's fence is symmetric in the quartiles, and a right-skewed distribution therefore has far more mass beyond the upper fence than beyond the lower one *by construction*, whatever the data. For a lognormal with sigma = 1 the standard fence flags about 8% of the sample on the right and essentially nothing on the left — and it does so for a perfectly clean sample. Read uncorrected, "8% of my cells are outliers" is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not about the cells.

records.source: **The asymmetry problem is real and is not fixed by choosing a bigger c.** Tukey's fence is symmetric in the quartiles, and a right-skewed distribution therefore has far more mass beyond the upper fence than beyond the lower one *by construction*, whatever the data. For a lognormal with sigma = 1 the standard fence flags about 8% of the sample on the right and essentially nothing on the left — and it does so for a perfectly clean sample. Read uncorrected, "8% of my cells are outliers" is a statement about the shape of the distribution, not about the cells.
records.translation: **El problema de la asimetría es real y no se resuelve eligiendo una c mayor.** La valla de Tukey es simétrica en los cuartiles, y por tanto una distribución asimétrica a la derecha tiene mucha más masa más allá de la valla superior que más allá de la inferior *por construcción*, sean cuales sean los datos. Para una lognormal con sigma = 1, la valla estándar señala aproximadamente el 8% de la muestra por la derecha y prácticamente nada por la izquierda, y lo hace con una muestra perfectamente limpia. Leído sin corregir, "el 8% de mis células son atípicas" es una afirmación sobre la forma de la distribución, no sobre las células.

records.context: The offered remedy is a **log10 transform**, :data:`TRANSFORM_LOG10`, which turns a lognormal into a Gaussian and makes the fence mean what it appears to mean. It is **never implicit**: a transform silently applied would change what ``outlier_score`` is in units of without the user asking. And it **refuses** rather than fudges on non-positive values — ``log10`` of a zero ``pathogen_area`` is ``-inf``, and an implicit ``+1`` or a dropped row would be an invented measurement or a self-selected population. The refusal names the feature and the count.

records.context: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#18
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why MCD and not an isolation forest.** Both are "multivariate outlier detectors" and they are not interchangeable:
records.translation: **Por qué MCD y no un bosque de aislamiento.** Ambos son "multivariate outlier detectors" (detectores multivariantes de valores atípicos) y no son intercambiables:

records.context: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model#19
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The threshold is a stated false-positive rate, not a tuned fraction.** Under multivariate normality the squared robust Mahalanobis distance is distributed chi-square with ``p`` degrees of freedom, so the cut point is ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` for a chosen ``alpha`` — default :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, meaning *one clean object in a thousand is expected to be flagged*. Over 10^5 objects that is about 100 false flags, and over the 200,000 objects of a typical two-plate screen it is about 200. That number is knowable in advance and is printed in :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. An isolation forest's score has no such null distribution and therefore no calibrated cut point at all.
records.translation: **El umbral es una tasa de falsos positivos declarada, no una fracción ajustada.** Bajo normalidad multivariante, la distancia de Mahalanobis robusta al cuadrado sigue una distribución chi-cuadrado con ``p`` grados de libertad, así que el punto de corte es ``chi2.ppf(1 - alpha, p)`` para un ``alpha`` elegido; por defecto :data:`DEFAULT_ALPHA` = 0.001, lo que significa que *se espera que se señale un objeto limpio de cada mil*. Sobre 10^5 objetos son unas 100 marcas falsas, y sobre los 200,000 objetos de un cribado típico de dos placas, unas 200. Ese número se conoce de antemano y se imprime en :meth:`OutlierResult.caveats`. La puntuación de un bosque de aislamiento no tiene ninguna distribución nula de este tipo y, por tanto, ningún punto de corte calibrado.

records.context: **Isolation forest requires** ``contamination`` — the share of the data that is bad — declared *in advance*. That share is precisely the unknown the analysis is trying to estimate. Setting ``contamination=0.01`` guarantees 1% of the objects come back flagged whether the plate is pristine or ruined, which makes the output uninterpretable in exactly the case it matters.

records.context: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **MCD is affine-equivariant.** Rescale ``area`` from px^2 to um^2, or rotate to any linear combination of the features, and the fitted centre and covariance transform with it: every distance, and so every flag, is unchanged. This is the same invariance argument :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` makes for standardising before a PCA, and it is why no scaling option is needed here — the metric *is* the covariance. A tree ensemble splits on raw coordinates and is not equivariant; its answer depends on the units.
records.translation: **MCD es equivariante afín.** Si se reescala ``area`` de px^2 a um^2, o se rota a cualquier combinación lineal de las características, el centro y la covarianza ajustados se transforman con ello: todas las distancias, y por tanto todas las marcas, quedan sin cambios. Es el mismo argumento de invariancia que :mod:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model` esgrime para estandarizar antes de un PCA, y es la razón por la que aquí no hace falta ninguna opción de escalado: la métrica *es* la covarianza. Un conjunto de árboles divide sobre coordenadas sin procesar y no es equivariante; su respuesta depende de las unidades.

records.context: **MCD is the multivariate generalisation of the median and the MAD.** The MCD centre is a multivariate median (the mean of the h-subset of minimum covariance determinant) and the MCD scatter is its spread. So all three methods offered here are the same idea at one, one, and p dimensions, and a user who understands the MAD already understands this.

Así, los tres métodos que se ofrecen aquí son la misma idea en una, una y p dimensiones, y un usuario que entiende la MAD ya entiende esto.

records.context: **The cost, stated.** MCD needs ``n > p`` to have a covariance at all, and it is unstable until roughly ``n >= 2p`` (:data:`MCD_MIN_OBJECTS_PER_FEATURE` * p): the estimate is fitted on a *subset* of about ``n/2`` rows, so ``n = 2p`` already means the subset is only barely larger than the dimension. Its breakdown point is set by ``support_fraction``: the sklearn default of ``(n + p + 1) / 2n`` gives the maximum ~50%, and raising it trades robustness for efficiency. Too few objects for the number of features is **refused with a message that names the way out**: run a PCA first (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.pca`) and flag on the first few components, which are fewer, uncorrelated, and carry the same information.

records.context: The whole-laboratory microplate failure that actually happens is a **bad microplate sample position**: one microplate sample position pipetted wrong, one microplate sample position out of focus, one microplate sample position where the cells were seeded at twice the density. records.translation: El fallo de placa completa que realmente ocurre es un **pocillo defectuoso**: un pocillo mal pipeteado, un pocillo desenfocado, un pocillo en el que las células se sembraron al doble de densidad. Las marcas por objeto son casi inútiles para encontrarlo, y la razón es aritmética, no de opinión.

records.context: Take 60 objects per well, a feature whose within-well spread is sigma, and a well whose whole population is shifted by 0.9 sigma. The **object** rule at k = 3.5 asks each object to exceed 3.5 sigma; a 0.9 sigma shift moves that requirement to 2.6 sigma, which about one object in 200 clears — so the bad well contributes a fraction of one extra flagged object and disappears into the ordinary tail. The **well** rule compares well *medians*, whose sampling spread is only ``1.2533 * sigma / sqrt(60) = 0.16 sigma``; the same shift is then 5.6 robust SDs and the well is unmistakable. The two tests have wildly different power against the same defect, which is why both are run and both are reported.

records.source: Take 60 objects per well, a feature whose within-well spread is sigma, and a well whose whole population is shifted by 0.9 sigma. The **well** rule compares well *medians*, whose sampling spread is only ``1.2533 * sigma / sqrt(60) = 0.16 sigma``; the same shift is then 5.6 robust SDs and the well is unmistakable. The two tests have wildly different power against the same defect, which is why both are run and both are reported.
records.translation: Tome 60 objetos por pocillo, una característica cuya dispersión dentro del pocillo es sigma, y un pocillo cuya población completa está desplazada 0.9 sigma. La regla de **objeto** con k = 3.5 exige que cada objeto supere 3.5 sigma; un desplazamiento de 0.9 sigma reduce esa exigencia a 2.6 sigma, que supera aproximadamente un objeto de cada 200, así que el pocillo defectuoso aporta una fracción de un objeto señalado adicional y desaparece en la cola ordinaria. La regla de **pocillo** compara las *medianas* de los pocillos, cuya dispersión muestral es solo ``1.2533 * sigma / sqrt(60) = 0.16 sigma``; el mismo desplazamiento equivale entonces a 5.6 SD robustas y el pocillo es inconfundible. Las dos pruebas tienen una potencia enormemente distinta frente al mismo defecto, y por eso se ejecutan y se notifican ambas.

records.context: So the microplate sample position pass is **not** "the microplate sample position contains many flagged objects". That statistic exists — it is reported as ``flagged_share`` — and it answers a different question: it finds a microplate sample position containing a few *catastrophic* objects (a segmentation blow-up, a piece of dust measured as a cell) while being blind to a uniform shift. The microplate sample position-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the microplate sample position frame because neither subsumes the other.

records.source: So the well pass is **not** "the well contains many flagged objects". That statistic exists — it is reported as ``flagged_share`` — and it answers a different question: it finds a well containing a few *catastrophic* objects (a segmentation blow-up, a piece of dust measured as a cell) while being blind to a uniform shift. The well-level robust score finds the uniform shift while being blind to the isolated catastrophe. Both are on the well frame because neither subsumes the other.
records.translation: Así pues, la pasada por pocillo **no** es "el pocillo contiene muchos objetos señalados". Ese estadístico existe (se notifica como ``flagged_share``) y responde a otra pregunta: encuentra un pocillo que contiene unos pocos objetos *catastróficos* (una segmentación desbocada, una mota de polvo medida como célula) pero es ciego a un desplazamiento uniforme. La puntuación robusta a nivel de pocillo encuentra el desplazamiento uniforme pero es ciega a la catástrofe aislada. Ambas están en el frame de pocillos porque ninguna engloba a la otra.
